# ui.tabs, run on every target: a tab is a record written as a child, and the
# panel is what the selected one was written with. The panel shown follows
# `selected`, a panel's handler writes the caller's state, and a `var` written
# in a panel is state of that panel.
#
# A test switches tabs as a user does, by pressing one: `c.strip.change(1)`
# clicks the tab at 1, which writes `selected` and fires @change. No node of
# the strip reports @change itself -- each tab's click emits it with its
# index -- so the trigger is a press of that tab (lower.NamePresses, and
# interp.View.Choosing on the interpreter), through the invoker each target
# has for one copy of a node a loop renders; it reaches through an instance
# too. A control in a panel that reports the same event -- a select's
# @change -- is the panel's writer's, and the trigger presses the tab all the
# same; two components each holding a `#strip` under one root are each
# pressed through their own.
#
# A loop in a panel makes copies a test indexes by that loop alone: the
# strip's loop over its tabs shows a tab's panel in one iteration, so it is no
# part of a copy's key (ir.RecordBranchOf), as the checker counts the ref --
# and the interpreter finds the loop in the panel, which is the population
# of the strip's hidden content slot.
#
# testdata/component_tabs.txtar is the code.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok   6 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok   6 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   6 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   6 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   6 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok   6 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component app ui.node {
    var idx = 0
    var hits = 0
    var changed = -1
    var rows = [1, 2, 3]
    var fruit = "Apple"
    ui.tabs #strip(:selected=idx, @change(i) {
        changed = i
    }) {
        ui.tab(label="One") {
            ui.button #hit(text="hit", @click {
                hits = hits + 1
            })
            ui.select(:value=fruit, @change(v) {
                hits = 100
            }) {
                ui.choice(label="Apple")
                ui.choice(label="Pear")
            }
        }
        ui.tab(label="Two") {
            var local = 0
            ui.button #twice(text="twice", @click {
                local = local + 1
                hits = local * 10
            })
            for var r = rows {
                ui.text #cell(value="row {r}")
            }
        }
    }
}

component wrapped ui.node {
    app #inner()
}

component pair ui.node {
    app #left()
    app #right()
}

func testTheSelectedPanelIsShown(t Test, c app) {
    t.assert(c.hit != null)
    if c.hit != null {
        c.hit.click()
    }
    t.assert(c.hits == 1)
}

func testSwitchingShowsAnotherPanel(t Test, c app) {
    c.strip.change(1)
    t.assert(c.idx == 1)
    t.assert(c.changed == 1)
    t.assert(c.hit == null)
    t.assert(c.twice != null)
    if c.twice != null {
        c.twice.click()
    }
    t.assert(c.hits == 10)
}

func testAPanelKeepsStateOfItsOwn(t Test, c app) {
    c.strip.change(1)
    t.assert(c.twice != null)
    if c.twice != null {
        c.twice.click()
        c.twice.click()
    }
    t.assert(c.hits == 20)
}

func testALoopInAPanelIsIndexedByItself(t Test, c app) {
    c.strip.change(1)
    t.assert(c.cell[0].value == "row 1")
    t.assert(c.cell[2].value == "row 3")
    t.assert(c.cell[3] == null)
}

func testTwoStripsArePressedEachThroughItsOwn(t Test, c pair) {
    c.right.strip.change(1)
    t.assert(c.right.idx == 1 && c.left.idx == 0)
    c.left.strip.change(1)
    t.assert(c.left.idx == 1 && c.left.hits == 0)
}

func testATabIsPressedThroughAnInstance(t Test, c wrapped) {
    c.inner.strip.change(1)
    t.assert(c.inner.idx == 1)
    t.assert(c.inner.changed == 1)
}

ui.window {
    app
}
